size.note: Newman's 45 cm. Mass: Newman's Birds gives 600–650 g.

habitat: Riparian forests, evergreen forest and heavily wooded regions; prefers light-barked trees such as baobabs; also edges of exotic plantations. Crepuscular (Newman's; SABAP1).

distribution.note: GBIF records per 10 000 bird records in each region: far north 1.2, north 0.56, central 0.19, south 1.6 (counted 13 November 2026). Recorded most often in the south.

summary: A dark-brown crepuscular hawk with pale yellow eyes and white legs; white throat with a dark mesial streak. Specialises on bats and swifts at dusk (Newman's).

similar.note: Kites are diurnal scavengers with forked tails; Bat Hawk has a square/rounded falcon-like outline at dusk (field guides).
